plan.title: Asked for a 5-minute version with a reason: set at once, spelled out in that text

context.text: Kalimera Jordan! Tonight at 8: scene 4 of Lighthouse in Notes, Theo walking back into Mara's bar, about 200 words in 20 minutes. Screenshot it when it's done. You in?

transcript.text: my kid's home sick and the full scene feels like too much today. can we make it easier, just 5 minutes? what's the smallest useful version I can do now?

Sick kid at home, so yes. Here's the small version, Jordan.

• Open Notes and write just the opening of Scene 4. Theo comes back to Mara's bar.
• About 60 words, 4 or 5 sentences. Don't worry about polish.
• Set a 5-minute timer and start now.
• Send me a screenshot of it in Notes when you're done.

A small version still counts and keeps your streak alive. Go take care of your kiddo, then knock this out. 💪

checks.reason: Names only a screenshot of the Notes writing as proof, with no typed text offered as proof.
Spells out what (opening of Scene 4), how much (about 60 words, 5-minute timer), when (start now) and proof (screenshot); not just 'set'.
The bullet list is fine, but about four sentences sit outside it (opener and closing), over the three-sentence limit.
Warm and sincere, acknowledges the sick kid without pushback, one emoji used as punctuation.

conversation.reason: With a real reason (sick kid), ZOH doesn't push back, sets a smaller version in one text, and spells out what, how much, when and screenshot proof.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression well: it accepted the real reason and spelled out a smaller Scene 4 step with what to write, how long, when to start and a Notes screenshot as proof, never just saying it was set. Its one weak spot is length, with a few sentences outside the bullet list that push past the short-text limit.
